thread:
emma_customer: Hey team — our trial credits show as expired this morning and it’s blocking our smoke tests. Account ac_42f9 (AcmeBots). We had a scheduled load test yesterday which should have consumed credits, but we expected an automatic promo reapply window. No extension was applied. Screenshot: https://imgur.com/example.jpg. Can someone confirm what happened and whether we can get a short grace reinstatement?

alice_support: Sorry you hit this, emma — I can look. Can you paste the promo code or promo id you used and the approximate time the test ran? Any x-request-id from API errors would help.

emma_customer: Promo code was TRIAL-ACME-2026, applied on 2026-02-15. Load test runs from ~2026-03-16T22:00 to 2026-03-17T01:00 UTC. Error in API response was just "quota_exceeded" in the UI, no helpful ID in the UI. I grabbed a few request-ids from our worker logs: req_64f1a9, req_64f1ab.

alice_support: Thanks. Escalating to eng and finance to check if the promo window logic failed and whether we can do a manual short-term grant. @mathew_engineer @clara_finance FYI.

infra_bot: [automated] billing-service: promo-apply failed -> 409 (promo_expired) for account ac_42f9; promo_id TRIAL-ACME-2026; request_ids: req_64f1a9, req_64f1ab; cluster: billing-us-west; trace: b89f3e

mathew_engineer: Looking. Two quick asks: 1) can you reproduce with a local curl against /v1/usage? e.g. ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/ac_42f9/usage``` 2) did you see any timezone or clock drift on your side? We sometimes have checks that consider UTC midnight and customer timezone shifts can cause off-by-one day expiry windows.

emma_customer: Running the curl now, will paste output in a minute. No intentional clock changes on our side; servers are in UTC.

ben_ce: Policy note: standard trial credits expire 30 days after grant. We can approve exceptions for active load tests or clear infra error — typically finance needs to approve a manual grant and we document the exception.

dave_csm: Suggest manual short grant while eng investigates root cause so their QA isn't blocked. If it's a bug we'll backfill usage.

clara_finance: I can approve a temporary patch credit while we investigate. I need the account id and a short justification (customer impacted, active load test, logs). If approved I'll create a manual credit tx and note it for audit.

alice_support: Emma — justification: active scheduled load test that should have fallen within promo reapply window; customer blocked from running CI and smoke tests. Can you confirm that's accurate?

emma_customer: Correct — we only ran the scheduled test and the UI showed expired credits. We couldn't run our end-to-end check which blocks our deploy.

clara_finance: Approved. Granting 10,000 trial token-equivalent credit to ac_42f9 as a temporary make-good while eng investigates. TX id: fin_tx_20260317_001. Please confirm once the customer sees the credit. I'll flag for reconciliation.

alice_support: Applied manual credit fin_tx_20260317_001 to ac_42f9. Can you refresh the UI and re-run the load test when ready, @emma_customer? Also assigning to @mathew_engineer to root-cause the promo reapply logic and file a follow-up.

mathew_engineer: Will take it. Initial hypothesis: expiry boundary check uses local date in a way that mis-evaluates promos when applied near midnight UTC; will add logging and a unit test. If we can get the curl output (usage + promo state) that helped earlier it’ll speed debugging.

emma_customer: I can confirm the credit appeared and the load test ran successfully after manual grant — thanks! Please keep me posted on root cause.

alice_support: Closing loop for now: manual credit applied, eng investigating potential expiry-window edge case, finance recorded TX. If you see any other failures please reopen. :thumbsup:
